quests.instruction: Blend /l/ /a/ /m/ /p/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: There are four sounds. Say each one, then glide them together.
quests.explanation: /l/ /a/ /m/ /p/ makes “lamp”. “Lap” is missing the /m/ and “limp” has a different vowel.
quests.funFact: Words with two consonant sounds at the end, like lamp, hand and milk, are sometimes called CVCC words.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with two consonant sounds, /n/ and /d/?
quests.hint: Listen to the very end of each word. You should hear two sounds after the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Hand” ends with /n/ and /d/ side by side. “Ham” and “hat” each end with a single consonant.

quests.instruction: Tap out the sounds in “milk”. How many taps are there?
quests.hint: Tap out each sound: /m/, the vowel, then the sounds at the end.
quests.explanation: “Milk” has 4 sounds: /m/ /i/ /l/ /k/. The last two sounds are a blend.

quests.instruction: Blend /s/ /w/ /i/ /m/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Check the vowel and the second sound before you choose.
quests.explanation: /s/ /w/ /i/ /m/ makes “swim”. “Slim” has /l/ in the second place and “swam” has a different vowel.
quests.funFact: “Swim” and “swam” are the same word at different times: now and earlier.

quests.instruction: Which sounds does “drop” break into?
quests.hint: Count the sounds before the vowel. There are two.
quests.explanation: “Drop” has four sounds: /d/ /r/ /o/ /p/. If you start with /t/ you would make “trop”.

quests.instruction: Which word has two consonant sounds, then a vowel, then one consonant sound?
quests.hint: Break each word into sounds and look at the pattern.
quests.explanation: “Snug” is /s/ /n/ /u/ /g/: two consonants, a vowel, then a consonant. “Sun” has only one consonant before the vowel, and “nest” has two at the end.

quests.instruction: How would you say the sounds in “frog” one by one?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. How many sounds are before the vowel?
quests.explanation: “Frog” has four sounds: /f/ /r/ /o/ /g/. If you add /l/ instead of /r/, you would say “flog”.

quests.instruction: Break “step” apart. Which sounds do you get?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and tap each sound.
quests.explanation: “Step” has four sounds: /s/ /t/ /e/ /p/. The vowel is short e.

quests.instruction: Which word has the sounds /s/ /t/ /a/ /m/ /p/?
quests.hint: The beginning and the ending are the same in all three words. Listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: /s/ /t/ /a/ /m/ /p/ makes “stamp”. “Stomp” has short o and “stump” has short u.
quests.funFact: Stamp, stomp and stump are a little set of words. Only the vowel changes.

quests.instruction: How many sounds do you hear in “crisp”?
quests.hint: Count each sound with a finger: /k/, /r/, the vowel, then the sounds at the end.
quests.explanation: “Crisp” has 5 sounds: /k/ /r/ /i/ /s/ /p/. Blends keep each sound separate.
quests.funFact: Crisp has five letters and five sounds, one for each letter.

quests.instruction: Which word has exactly four sounds?
quests.hint: Count the sounds in each word. Remember that sh is one sound.
quests.explanation: “Desk” has 4 sounds: /d/ /e/ /s/ /k/. “Dish” and “dog” each have 3.

quests.instruction: Which word has MORE sounds than “net”?
quests.hint: Count the sounds in net, then check which word is longer by sound.
quests.explanation: “Net” has 3 sounds. “Nest” has 4 because it adds /s/ before the /t/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the blend /n/ + /d/?
quests.hint: Listen to the last two sounds. A tongue tap follows the /n/.
quests.explanation: “Sand” ends with /n/ and /d/. “Sat” ends with one sound and “sang” ends with /ng/.
quests.funFact: Sand, hand, band and land all end with -and.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /s/ + /t/?
quests.hint: Listen for a hiss followed by a quick tap at the end.
quests.explanation: “Nest” ends with /s/ and /t/. “Net” only has /t/ and “neck” ends with /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /m/ + /p/?
quests.hint: Your lips close for /m/ and pop for /p/.
quests.explanation: “Jump” ends with /m/ and /p/. “Jug” ends with /g/ and “just” ends with /s/ and /t/.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /b/ /e/ /l/ /t/?
quests.hint: Match each sound to a letter. Check that none is missing.
quests.explanation: “Belt” has four sounds that match b-e-l-t. “Bell” has 3 sounds and “bet” has 3 sounds.
quests.funFact: Belt, bell and bet all start with the same two sounds, /b/ and /e/.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /p/ /o/ /n/ /d/?
quests.hint: Count the sounds. There should be two at the end.
quests.explanation: “Pond” has four sounds that match p-o-n-d. “Pod” has 3, and “pound” has a different vowel sound.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /d/ /u/ /s/ /t/?
quests.hint: Compare the last sound. Is it /t/ or /k/?
quests.explanation: “Dust” ends with /s/ and /t/. “Dusk” ends with /s/ and /k/, and “duct” ends with /k/ and /t/.

quests.instruction: Blend /p/ /l/ /a/ /n/ /t/. Which word is it?
quests.hint: There are five sounds. Say them one at a time.
quests.explanation: /p/ /l/ /a/ /n/ /t/ makes “plant”. “Plan” is missing the final /t/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the sounds /t/ /w/ /i/ /s/ /t/?
quests.hint: Start with the first two sounds, then check the end.
quests.explanation: “Twist” is /t/ /w/ /i/ /s/ /t/. “Twin” is missing the last two sounds and “wrist” starts with /r/.
quests.funFact: In “wrist”, the w is silent. You say /r/ at the start.

quests.instruction: Which sound is missing? /f/ /r/ /o/ ? /t/ makes the word “frost”.
quests.hint: Say the whole word out loud and listen to what comes before the final /t/.
quests.explanation: “Frost” is /f/ /r/ /o/ /s/ /t/. The missing sound is /s/, which blends with /t/ at the end.

quests.instruction: Which word has the pattern consonant, consonant, vowel, consonant, like “trap”?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly and sort its sounds into consonants and vowels.
quests.explanation: “Snip” is /s/ /n/ /i/ /p/, the same pattern as “trap”. “Nest” has two consonants at the end, and “stamp” has five sounds.
quests.funFact: Snip, trap and frog are all CCVC words: two consonants, a vowel, then one consonant.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with two consonant sounds?
quests.hint: Listen to the ending of each word. Count the sounds after the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Tent” ends with /n/ and /t/. “Ten” ends with /n/, and “tell” ends with /l/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same last two sounds as “jump”?
quests.hint: Say the last two sounds of jump. Then match them.
quests.explanation: “Jump” and “lamp” both end with /m/ and /p/. “List” ends with /s/ and /t/, and “lung” ends with /ng/.

quests.instruction: Count the sounds in “drift”, including both blends.
quests.hint: Count each sound. There are two at the start and two at the end.
quests.explanation: “Drift” has 5 sounds: /d/ /r/ /i/ /f/ /t/.

quests.instruction: Which word has 4 sounds, even though it has 5 letters?
quests.hint: Remember that a digraph is one sound. Look for one in these words.
quests.explanation: “Chimp” has /ch/ /i/ /m/ /p/, 4 sounds, because ch is one sound. “Blend” and “crisp” have 5 sounds.
quests.funFact: In “chimp”, ch makes one sound, so the word has five letters but only four sounds.

quests.instruction: Which word has exactly 5 sounds?
quests.hint: Count carefully. A digraph counts as one sound, but a blend counts as two.
quests.explanation: “Blast” is /b/ /l/ /a/ /s/ /t/, five sounds. “Chest” and “brush” each have 4 because of their digraphs.

quests.instruction: Blend /s/ /l/ /e/ /d/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Say each sound slowly, then blend them. Listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: /s/ /l/ /e/ /d/ makes “sled”. “Slid” has short i and “sad” is missing the /l/.
quests.funFact: Sled, slid and slip all start with the blend sl.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT have exactly 4 sounds?
quests.hint: Count the sounds in each word and see which one is different.
quests.explanation: “Milk” and “step” each have 4 sounds. “Tub” has 3 sounds.

quests.instruction: Final check: how many sounds are in “stamp”?
quests.hint: Take your time and tap each sound: two at the start, a vowel, then two at the end.
quests.explanation: “Stamp” has 5 sounds: /s/ /t/ /a/ /m/ /p/. Words like this can look short but need careful listening.
